findings.text: Custom __rich_repr__ methods lose angular support: the code only sets __rich_repr__.angular when auto-generating the method (line 122), but classes with custom __rich_repr__ that set __rich_repr__.angular = True will have getattr return False, breaking angular bracket output.

Auto-generated __rich_repr__ assumes all __init__ parameters are stored as instance attributes; if a parameter like 'password' is accepted but not stored as self.password, getattr(self, name) will raise AttributeError at runtime.
The bare except with 'from None' swallows the original exception traceback, making debugging harder when inspect.signature fails for unexpected reasons like malformed __init__ annotations.

0.reason: The code only sets __rich_repr__.angular when auto-generating the method, but custom __rich_repr__ methods that set angular=True will still have getattr return True because the attribute is set on the function object itself, not overwritten by the decorator.

1.reason: The auto-generated __rich_repr__ uses getattr(self, name) for every __init__ parameter, which will raise AttributeError if a parameter is not stored as an instance attribute.

2.reason: The bare except with 'from None' is intentional to raise a ReprError with a clean message, and the original traceback is not required for the functionality.
